0.0.n: Introduces an example supporting the speaker’s point.

0.1.n: Sets the time period being discussed.

0.2.n: Marks 昔 as the topic, contrasting past attitudes with the present.

0.4.n: The て-form of 勉強する links studying to the actions that follow.

0.5.n: Describes 学校 as desirable or well regarded.

0.6.n: Refers to the school someone attends.

0.7.n: Marks 学校 as the destination of 行って.

0.8.n: The て-form of 行く connects attending school with joining a company.

0.10.n: Describes 会社 as a desirable employer.

0.11.n: Refers to the employer someone joins after school.

0.12.n: Marks 会社 as the organization someone enters.

0.13.n: 入る with 会社 means becoming an employee, not simply entering a building.

0.14.n: Turns the preceding chain of actions into something that can serve as the subject.

0.15.n: Marks the whole study-school-company path as what was judged good.

0.16.n: The spelling 善い emphasizes moral approval rather than simply high quality.

0.17.n: Combines with 善い to describe the preceding actions as something morally approved.

0.18.n: Marks the judgment being reported by 言われていました.

0.19.n: Polite past form of 言われている; the passive form reports a commonly expressed view.

1.0.n: Connects this social judgment to the previous example.

1.2.n: Pairs with できなかった to describe difficulty doing well academically.

1.3.n: Past negative of できる; before 人, it describes people who struggled academically.

1.4.n: The preceding phrase 勉強できなかった identifies which people are being discussed.

1.5.n: Marks people who struggled academically as the topic of the judgment that follows.

1.6.n: Combines with に to describe the standpoint from which people were judged.

1.7.n: Makes 社会的 describe how or from what perspective someone is 良くない.

1.8.n: Negative form of 良い, directly describing 人.

1.9.n: Labels the topic group negatively; the sentence continues into the next line.

2.0.n: Introduces a stronger restatement of the preceding negative judgment.

2.1.n: A noun expressing moral condemnation, stronger than simply being inadequate.

2.2.n: Part of である, the formal written-style equivalent of だ.

2.3.n: Completes である; together they assert that someone is 悪.

2.4.n: Marks 悪である as the content of what people thought.

2.5.n: Past form of 考えられている; the passive form describes a view held about these people.

2.6.n: Packages the statement as an explanation, together with です.

2.7.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory ending のです.

0.lit: For example, formerly, studying, going to a good school, and joining a good company were said to be good things.
0.tip: の turns the entire chain of actions into the subject marked by が.

1.lit: And, as for people who could not study well, socially not-good people,
1.tip: 勉強できなかった comes before 人 to describe which people the speaker means.

2.lit: In other words, they were considered to be evil, you see.
2.tip: と考えられていた reports a past belief held about people, not necessarily the speaker’s own view.
